WELCOME.TITLE: Create a candidate
WELCOME.TEXT: This form creates a candidate in 4 steps. Nothing is saved before the last step. Follow this guide to discover each part.

IDENTITY.TITLE: 1. Identity Information
IDENTITY.TEXT: First name, last name and email (a valid address) are required. Phone, date of birth, gender, national ID, passport and location are optional: they are carried over to the HR profile at hiring.

POSITION.TITLE: 2. Position & Contract
POSITION.TEXT: Start with « Hiring request »: picking an open position fills the position, start date, department, grade and discipline still empty. Contract type and start date are required. Salary information is optional.

CV_NOTES.TITLE: 3. CV and 4. Notes
CV_NOTES.TEXT: Drop the CV (PDF, DOC or DOCX, 10 MB at most), then add your notes and comments. Both are optional: the CV can also be added later from the candidate's page.

PROGRESS.TITLE: Progress and profile quality
PROGRESS.TEXT: « Progress » shows the current step and the completed ones. « Profile quality » shows the share of fields filled in (CV included) and ticks the key information: name, email, position, contract and start date.

ACTIONS.TITLE: Move on and save
ACTIONS.TEXT: « Next » goes to the next step; it stays greyed out while a required field is missing, and a message says which. « Previous » goes back without losing anything. On the last step, « Save the profile » creates the candidate and opens their page. « Cancel » drops what you typed.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Candidates » tab. You will also find this form's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: A candidate's file
WELCOME.TEXT: This file holds the whole record of a candidate, from application to hiring. Follow this guide to discover each part; it opens the tabs for you.

HEADER.TITLE: File actions
HEADER.TEXT: Top right, depending on the stage and your rights: « Accept » and « Reject » for a pending candidate, « IT Provisioning » during IT preparation, « Complete onboarding », « Hire », then « View profile » once the candidate is hired.

IDENTITY.TITLE: The identity card
IDENTITY.TEXT: On the left: the candidate's status, contract and contact details. With the right to edit, « Edit » makes the identity and the Profile tab editable; a bar appears at the bottom to « Save ». A hired candidate is no longer edited here, but in their employee profile.

RAIL.TITLE: Where the candidate stands
RAIL.TEXT: The rail follows the hiring steps: Pending, Accepted, Offer sent, IT in progress, Email received, HR in progress and Hired, with the date each step was reached.

PROFILE.TITLE: Profile
PROFILE.TEXT: The position applied for, the recruitment request (or « Unsolicited application »), the contract, department, grade, experience, expected start date and notes.

SALARY.TITLE: Compensation
SALARY.TEXT: The HR budget and the candidate's expectation (net), with their own « Save » button, then the employer cost simulation. This tab only shows with the right to hire or for an administrator.

INTERVIEWS.TITLE: Interviews
INTERVIEWS.TEXT: « Schedule » adds an interview (type, date, time, place, interviewers). Once held, mark it « Passed » or « Failed » with your notes, or cancel it. A « Join on Teams » link shows for an online interview.

OFFER.TITLE: Offer
OFFER.TEXT: Once the candidate is accepted: « Prepare the offer », « Cost it » (the proposed salary), then « Submit for approval ». Once budget control approves the cost, « Send to candidate ». Each renegotiation creates a new proposal, kept in the history.

CV.TITLE: CV
CV.TEXT: Download the CV or replace it (PDF, DOC or DOCX, 10 MB at most). Without a CV, « Add a CV » lets you upload one.

IT.TITLE: IT provisioning
IT.TEXT: After acceptance: the progress of the IT preparation, with the account, equipment and licences. With the IT right, « Manage provisioning » opens the IT file.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Candidates » tab, opened from a candidate's file. You will also find this file's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Welcome to IT Provisioning
WELCOME.TEXT: This page lists the IT files still open: each new employee to equip (Microsoft 365 account, hardware, licences, Active Directory). Completed files move to « History ».

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: « Pending files », « Overdue » (start date passed), « Incomplete hardware » and « Incomplete licenses ». They cover all open files: search and filters don't change them.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search, filters and display
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search by candidate, position or email. « Filters » lets you pick a status, the missing items (hardware, licences, MS365 email), an AD profile, a position, a start date or overdue files. The icons on the right switch between grid and list.

ITEMS.TITLE: The files
ITEMS.TEXT: Each file shows the candidate, their MS365 email, the status (Pending, In progress, Email created), the start date with any delay, and the progress of hardware and licences. Click a file to work on it.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « IT Provisioning » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Provisioning history
WELCOME.TEXT: Here are the completed IT files, newest first. Click a file to view it or download its hardware discharge.

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: « Completed files », « Completed this month » and « Average lead time (days) », the average time between a file's creation and its completion. They cover the whole history, not the search.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search and filters
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search by candidate, position or email. « Filters » lets you pick the completion date, who completed it, an AD profile, a position or a start date.

ITEMS.TITLE: Completed files
ITEMS.TEXT: Same cards and list as the open files. Click a file to open it; the breadcrumb then brings you back to the history.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « IT Provisioning » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: A candidate's IT file
WELCOME.TEXT: This file is handled in 6 steps, in any order. Follow this guide: it opens each step for you.

PROGRESS.TITLE: Progress
PROGRESS.TEXT: The right column shows the 6 steps; a green tick marks a filled step. Click a step to go straight to it.

IDENTITY.TITLE: 1. Identity
IDENTITY.TEXT: The candidate's information from recruitment: name, position, expected start date and status. Nothing to enter here.

MS365.TITLE: 2. Microsoft 365
MS365.TEXT: Enter the work address (firstname.lastname@itecgroupe.com), then « Submit email » and « Confirm creation ». This creates the employee's account in DAF360: it is irreversible, check the address first.

HARDWARE.TITLE: 3. Hardware
HARDWARE.TEXT: Tick « Provided » for each item handed over, then fill in the serial number, brand / model, Asset Tag and condition. Unticking an item clears its details. Hardware notes are free text.

LICENSES.TITLE: 4. Licenses
LICENSES.TEXT: Tick the licences granted: Office 365, AutoCAD, Revit, Autodesk and Kaspersky. Other software goes in « Other licenses ».

AD.TITLE: 5. Active Directory
AD.TEXT: Tick « Active Directory account created » once the account is made, and pick the « AD profile type ».

NOTES.TITLE: 6. Notes & Finalization
NOTES.TEXT: Add your general notes. Once the file is completed, « Generate discharge » produces the hardware handover document for the employee.

ACTIONS.TITLE: Save and finish
ACTIONS.TEXT: « Previous » and « Next » change step without losing anything. « Save draft » stores what you entered: do it before leaving the page. On the last step, « Mark as completed » closes the file; the MS365 email and the AD account are needed first.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « IT Provisioning » tab, opened from an IT file.

WELCOME.TITLE: Welcome to HR Onboarding
WELCOME.TEXT: Here are the new employees whose IT account is ready and whose HR file is still to complete. Once the file is created, the employee leaves this list and shows in « Profiles ».

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: « Employees pending », « Profiles created today », « Incomplete profiles » and « Average creation time », the average time to fill a file (under 30 min: fast pace).

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search, filters and display
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search by employee, position or email. « Filters » lets you pick a status, started or untouched files (« Draft »), a start date, passed start dates and, if you manage several, an entity. The icons on the right switch between grid and list.

ITEMS.TITLE: The files
ITEMS.TEXT: Each file shows the employee, their MS365 email, the IT status, the expected start date and the last update; the « Draft » badge marks a file already started. Click a file to complete it.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Onboarding » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: The onboarding file
WELCOME.TEXT: This file creates the new employee's HR profile, in 8 steps. Follow this guide: it opens each step for you, without saving anything.

CARD.TITLE: The employee
CARD.TEXT: On the left: the photo (the camera icon changes it), then the information prepared by IT — employee ID, work email, PC, licence — read-only. Below, the « Onboarding status » follows the main steps of their arrival.

STEPPER.TITLE: The 8 steps
STEPPER.TEXT: Identity, Position, Contract, Regime, Personal, Bank, Emergency and Summary. Click a step to go straight to it: you can fill them in any order.

IDENTITY.TITLE: 1. Identity
IDENTITY.TEXT: Name, date of birth, gender, nationality, national ID and passport, taken from the application: check them and correct if needed.

POSITION.TITLE: 2. Position
POSITION.TEXT: The hire date and contract type (required), grade, discipline, department, NOG level, and the probation period with its end date.

CONTRACT.TITLE: 3. Contract
CONTRACT.TEXT: On the left, what was negotiated during recruitment (offer, salaries, approvals, interviews), read-only. On the right, what you validate: the notice period and the agreed net salary, prefilled from the offer. Also attach the signed contract (PDF, 10 MB).

REGIME.TITLE: 4. Regime
REGIME.TEXT: Pick the work regime (hours per week) and its start date. Required.

PERSONAL.TITLE: 5. Personal
PERSONAL.TEXT: The social security number (required) and its affiliation date, marital status, number of children, personal phone and address.

BANK.TITLE: 6. Bank
BANK.TEXT: The bank, the RIB (required), account number, IBAN, social insurance and tax numbers, and the bank certificate to attach (required: PDF, JPG or PNG, 10 MB).

EMERGENCY.TITLE: 7. Emergency
EMERGENCY.TEXT: The person to contact in an emergency: name, relationship and phone. Optional.

SUMMARY.TITLE: 8. Summary
SUMMARY.TEXT: All the information entered, by block; « Edit » takes you back to the step. Read it over before submitting.

ACTIONS.TITLE: Save and submit
ACTIONS.TEXT: « Save Draft » stores what you entered to resume later. On the last step, « Submit and create the file » checks the required fields, asks for confirmation, then creates the employee's profile and sends them a welcome email.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Onboarding » tab, opened from a file.

WELCOME.TITLE: Welcome to Offboarding
WELCOME.TEXT: This page follows employee departures, from the open file to its closure. An offboarding is started from the employee's profile (« Start offboarding »); here you follow and open the files.

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: « Active files », « Blocked » (a mandatory task overdue), « SLA breached » and « Validated » (closed files). On a per-reason page, such as « Resignation », they only count that reason; search and filters don't change them.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search, filters and display
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search by employee, reason or manager. « Filters » lets you pick a status, a departure reason, a last-working-day range, or only late or SLA-breached files. The icons on the right switch between kanban and list view.

BOARD.TITLE: The files
BOARD.TEXT: In kanban view, the 7 columns are the departure stages: Declaration, Validation, Handover, IT & Assets, HR Kit, Payroll & Settlement and Closure. They are derived from the tasks: cards are not dragged. Click a file to move it forward.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Offboarding » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: The departure file
WELCOME.TEXT: This file follows an employee's departure in 7 stages, each held by its department (HR, manager, IT, finance). Follow this guide: it opens each stage for you, without changing anything.

HEADER.TITLE: File actions
HEADER.TEXT: Top right: « History » opens the log of every action. Depending on your rights and the file's state: « Validate offboarding » (closure), « Cancel » (cancels the whole departure), then « Reopen » or « Archive » once the file is closed.

CARD.TITLE: The employee
CARD.TEXT: On the left: the reason, the file status (and « SLA breached » if so), the last working day, the trigger date and the person responsible for the handover.

RAIL.TITLE: The 7 stages
RAIL.TEXT: Click a stage to open it; a green stage is done, a locked stage can't be opened yet. Below, the task progress and the « Next step » to do.

DECLARATION.TITLE: 1. Departure declaration
DECLARATION.TEXT: The reason, notification date, notice period and supporting document. « Complete the declaration » lets you enter the last working day (required), the notice waiver, the resignation letter and notes. Until the last day is set, the next stages stay locked.

VALIDATION.TITLE: 2. Manager & HR validation
VALIDATION.TEXT: First the manager's decision (« Record the manager's decision »), then the HR validation (« Validate (HR) ») with the final end date and, if any, the notice paid but not worked. Stages 3 to 7 open once HR has validated.

HANDOVER.TITLE: 3. Handover & succession
HANDOVER.TEXT: « Name a successor », the handover period, the checklist of items to hand over and the handover minutes (to upload or write).

IT_ASSETS.TITLE: 4. IT & equipment
IT_ASSETS.TEXT: The equipment to return: tick each return (« Confirm the return », final), pick it up with « Sync from IT » or « Add an asset ». Schedule the account deactivation, then « Generate discharge form ».

HR_DOCS.TITLE: 5. HR management & documents
HR_DOCS.TEXT: The exit interview (« Schedule », then « Record the outcome »), and the HR kit: generate each document (work certificate…), then « Download the full HR kit ».

PAYROLL.TITLE: 6. Payroll & final settlement
PAYROLL.TEXT: The final settlement lines (« Propose the lines » or « Add a line »), the net total and the planned payment date. « Validate settlement » stays greyed out while a blocking task of another stage is open.

CLOSURE.TITLE: 7. File closure
CLOSURE.TEXT: « Validate offboarding » locks the file and moves the employee's profile to « Terminated ». Only possible once no blocking task is left open.

BAR.TITLE: Moving through the file
BAR.TEXT: At the bottom, the buttons on each side of « Step x of 7 » go to the previous or next stage. The next button is greyed out while the following stage is still locked.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Offboarding » tab, opened from a departure file.

WELCOME.TITLE: Requests to handle
WELCOME.TEXT: Here are the leave requests you are the manager (or deputy) for. The list opens on « Pending » requests: it is your decision queue.

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: « Total » (every request in your queue, all statuses), « Pending », « Approved » and « Refused ». They follow neither the search nor the page shown.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search, filters and display
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search for an employee or a reason. « Filter » lets you pick a status (Pending, Approved, Rejected, Archived), a leave type and a period. The icons on the right switch between « Cards » and « Table ». With the « Pending » status, « Approve all » approves the whole filtered queue at once.

ITEMS.TITLE: The requests
ITEMS.TEXT: Each request shows the employee, type, period, days and status. On a pending request: « Approve » (the days are debited from the balance) or « Reject » (a reason is required). A click opens the detail, with the supporting document and the employee's balances.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Leave » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Back-dated entries
WELCOME.TEXT: A back-dated entry is a leave filed on an employee's behalf, often after the fact (they didn't file it themselves). It then goes through approval like any request.

NEW.TITLE: New entry
NEW.TEXT: « New entry », top right, opens the form: employee, leave type, duration, dates, manager, supporting document if the type requires it, and the reason for the entry.

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: « Back-dated entries » (all those filed, all statuses), « Pending », « Approved » and « Refused ».

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search, filters and display
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search for an employee or a reason. « Filter » lets you pick a status (Pending, Approved, Rejected, Archived), a leave type and a period. The icons on the right switch between « Cards » and « Table ». The « Everyone's entries » / « My entries » button switches between your entries and everyone's: it shows the view it switches to.

ITEMS.TITLE: Filed entries
ITEMS.TEXT: Each row also shows who filed it (« Filed by »). A click opens the request's detail.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Leave » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: My team's leave
WELCOME.TEXT: The history of your team's requests, that is everyone below you in the hierarchy. This page is for viewing: decisions are made in « To handle ».

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: « Total », « Pending », « Approved » and « Archived », over your whole team.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search, filters and display
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search for an employee or a reason. « Filter » lets you pick a status (Pending, Approved, Rejected, Archived), a leave type and a period. The icons on the right switch between « Cards » and « Table ».

ITEMS.TITLE: The requests
ITEMS.TEXT: Newest first. A click opens the detail: period, days, duration, manager, supporting document, reason and, if any, the reason for rejection.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Leave » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: All leave
WELCOME.TEXT: The history of every request in the countries your role covers. This is also where a request is archived.

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: « Total », « Pending », « Approved » and « Archived », over your whole scope.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search, filters and display
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search for an employee or a reason. « Filter » lets you pick a status (Pending, Approved, Rejected, Archived), a leave type and a period. The icons on the right switch between « Cards » and « Table ».

ITEMS.TITLE: The requests
ITEMS.TEXT: A click opens the detail. « Archive » removes a request from the active lists; if it was approved, its days are credited back to the employee. Archiving can't be undone.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Leave » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: The request inbox
WELCOME.TEXT: Here are your entity's HR requests still open (certificates, data changes, training…): « Submitted », « In progress » or « Awaiting L2 ». Once decided, they move to the request history.

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: « In progress », « Urgent », « To handle soon » and « On track ». Urgency is computed from the submission date: a request becomes urgent after 3 days.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search, filters and display
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search by employee name. « Filters » lets you pick the urgency, request type, status and submission date. The icons on the right switch between « Card view » and « Table view ».

ITEMS.TITLE: The requests
ITEMS.TEXT: Each request shows the employee, type, status, reference and urgency. « Approve the request » approves it directly; to reject, open the request (« View detail »). The requester can « Cancel request » while it is « Submitted ».

RECRUITMENT.TITLE: Hiring requests
RECRUITMENT.TEXT: With the right to approve hiring, the « Recruitment » tab lists the pending position requests: « Approve » or « Reject » (the reason for rejection is required). You never approve your own request.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Requests » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: An HR request's detail
WELCOME.TEXT: The request type, its date and status, the requester, the reason, the attachments and the request's history.

HEADER.TITLE: The header
HEADER.TEXT: « Take charge » takes you to the decision block. The breadcrumb brings you back to the inbox, or to the history if you came from there.

ACTION.TITLE: Processing action
ACTION.TEXT: Enter a « Comment » (required), then « Approve » or « Reject ». There is no confirmation: the decision is final.

CONTENT.TITLE: Reason, documents and history
CONTENT.TEXT: On the right: the « Reason for request », the « Attachments » to download, the « Generated documents », then the « History » of the steps (submission, processing, decision).

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Requests » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: The request history
WELCOME.TEXT: The requests already decided. Two tabs: « Request » (approved, rejected, cancelled) and « Recruitment ».

TABS.TITLE: The two tabs
TABS.TEXT: « Request » for employees' requests, « Recruitment » for the position requests. Each tab has its own counters, search and filters.

OTHER.TITLE: Handled HR requests
OTHER.TEXT: Search by employee name; « Filters » lets you pick the status, type, submission date and decision date. A click opens the request.

RECRUITMENT.TITLE: Handled hiring requests
RECRUITMENT.TEXT: Search by position or department; « Filters » lets you pick the status (Approved, Rejected, Cancelled, Closed), department, reason and date. A click opens the request.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Requests » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: A hiring request
WELCOME.TEXT: The requested position: « Position details » on the left (reason, headcount, urgency, level, start date, linked candidates), the decision and the description of the need on the right.

HEADER.TITLE: The header
HEADER.TEXT: The position title, its department and the request status. The breadcrumb brings you back to the history or the inbox.

DECIDE.TITLE: Process the request
DECIDE.TEXT: For a « Pending » request that isn't yours: « Process the request », an optional comment, then « Approve » or « Reject ». The creator can « Cancel this request » while it is pending.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Requests » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Moves to CDI
WELCOME.TEXT: This page follows the requests to move a CIVP to a CDI: technical and salary validation, possible escalation, then the contract conversion by HR. A request is filed from the employee's profile.

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: « Waiting for me », « Awaiting decision », « Approved, to convert » and « Converted to CDI ».

TABS.TITLE: The two tabs
TABS.TEXT: « To handle »: what waits for your action given your role (a request to validate, an escalated request, or a contract to draw up). « All requests »: every request in your scope.

TABLE.TITLE: The requests
TABLE.TEXT: Each row shows the employee, the status (To validate, Escalated, Approved — to convert, Converted to CDI, Rejected, Cancelled), the CDI start date, the net salary, the requester and the filing date. A click opens the request.

DRAWER.TITLE: A request's detail
DRAWER.TEXT: The panel that opens shows the request (proposed salary, justification, evaluation file), the decision and the history. Depending on your role: « Approve », « Reject », « Escalate » or « Cancel request ». « Open profile » leads to the employee.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Moves to CDI » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Your team's missions
WELCOME.TEXT: Here you plan your team's missions and follow those still being validated (« Awaiting HR » or « Awaiting finance »). Handled missions move to « Mission history ».

NEW.TITLE: New mission
NEW.TEXT: « New mission », top right, opens the « Plan a mission » form: employee, subject, dates, type, destination and owner. It then goes to HR.

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: « Awaiting HR », « Awaiting finance », « Upcoming » (approved missions not started yet) and « Late » (departure passed while the mission is still awaiting a validation).

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search, filters and display
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search for an employee, a subject, a city or a country. « Filter » lets you pick a status, an employee, the scope (national or international) and a period. The icons on the right switch between « Card view » and « List view ».

ITEMS.TITLE: The missions
ITEMS.TEXT: Each mission shows the employee, subject, destination, period and estimated cost (or « Costs to enter »). « View details » opens the mission; while it is « Awaiting HR », the red icon lets you cancel it.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Missions » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Mission history
WELCOME.TEXT: Missions already handled: approved, rejected by HR or by finance, or cancelled. This page is for viewing.

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: « Closed missions », « Approved », « Rejected » (by HR or finance) and « Cancelled ».

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search, filters and display
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search for an employee, a subject, a city or a country. « Filter » lets you pick a status, an employee, the scope (national or international) and a period. The icons on the right switch between « Card view » and « List view ». The filter also offers the destination country.

ITEMS.TITLE: Closed missions
ITEMS.TEXT: A click opens the detail: the mission, the costs entered by HR and the history of decisions, with their reasons.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Missions » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Ticketing
WELCOME.TEXT: HR's desk for missions: price the missions submitted by managers, approve or reject them, and answer employees' change or cancellation requests.

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: « Missions to handle », « Expenses missing », « Departures passed » (the departure has passed while the mission is still waiting) and « Employee requests ».

TABS.TITLE: The two tabs
TABS.TEXT: « To handle »: the missions submitted by managers, to price then approve. « Requests »: employees' period-change or cancellation requests.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search and filters
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search for an employee, a subject or a city. « Filter » lets you pick missions whose expenses are missing or already entered, an employee, a country and a period. The icons on the right switch between cards and list.

ITEMS.TITLE: Missions to handle
ITEMS.TEXT: Each mission shows the employee, destination, period, departure (in N days or late) and estimated cost. The icons: « View details », « Fill in the expenses », « Approve and send to finance » (once the expenses are entered) and « Reject the mission ».

PRICE.TITLE: Fill in the expenses
PRICE.TEXT: The « Mission expenses » window: the currency (required), the daily allowance and the total amount (« Apply » computes allowance × days), lodging, transport (ticket, times), additional costs (visa, insurance) and the advance handed to the employee. The « Total estimated cost » updates live. « Save expenses » does not approve the mission yet.

DECIDE.TITLE: Approve or reject
DECIDE.TEXT: « Approve and send to finance » (optional comment) sends the mission to finance for the final decision. « Reject the mission » asks for a reason and closes the mission. Both are final.

REQUESTS.TITLE: Employees' requests
REQUESTS.TEXT: Each row gives the mission, the type (« Period change » or cancellation), the requested period and the reason. « Accept the request » applies straight away, without confirmation; « Refuse the request » asks for a reason.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Ticketing » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Administration
WELCOME.TEXT: The HR module's settings for your entity: roles, users, public holidays, leave and request types, lists, notifications… Each card opens a section.

HEADER.TITLE: The entity
HEADER.TEXT: The subtitle shows the entity (country) being configured. If you manage several entities, « Change country » switches to another.

CARDS.TITLE: The sections
CARDS.TEXT: One card per section you are allowed to manage. Click to open it; the « Administration » breadcrumb brings you back to the cards. The address keeps the open section (?tab=…), handy for a bookmark.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Roles & Permissions
WELCOME.TEXT: A role groups permissions, and each user has a single role. Their role's permissions are what open the HR module's menus, pages and buttons.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search for a role by name. On the right, reset the sort or choose the columns shown.

NEW.TITLE: New role
NEW.TEXT: Opens role creation: the name (required), the English name (optional, shown when the interface is in English), the parent role and the country scope. « Create role » opens it right away, so you can give it its permissions.

TABLE.TITLE: The roles
TABLE.TEXT: Each row shows the role's number of permissions and users, and its scope when it goes beyond the user's own country (« View all » or « N countries »). Click a role to open it.

END_LIST.TEXT: Open a role, then replay this guide from « Help & guides »: it then presents the role's three tabs. You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

ROLE.TITLE: An open role
ROLE.TEXT: Three tabs: « Information », « Permissions » and « Users ». In the breadcrumb, « Roles & Permissions » goes back to the list and « Administration » to the cards.

INFO.TITLE: The information
INFO.TEXT: The name, the English name and the parent role. The parent role places the role in the hierarchy: holders of the parent role are the managers of this role's holders (leave approval, notifications sent to the « manager »). « Save » applies; renaming a role already assigned asks for confirmation.

SCOPE.TITLE: The country scope
SCOPE.TEXT: « User's country »: each holder only sees their own country's data. « Defined list of countries »: all holders see the same countries, picked in « Visible countries ». « All countries »: no filter.

DELETE.TITLE: Deleting a role
DELETE.TEXT: « Delete this role », at the bottom of the tab, asks for confirmation and cannot be undone. The button stays greyed out while active users hold the role: give them another role first.

PERMISSIONS.TITLE: The permissions
PERMISSIONS.TEXT: Permissions are grouped by area; click a group to collapse it. Ticking or unticking a box saves it at once. « Select all » and « Deselect all » only change the display: then click « Save all ».

USERS.TITLE: The users
USERS.TEXT: The role's holders, with a filter. « Add a user » searches for an account by name or email; « Assign » gives them this role in place of their current one (shown as a badge). A row's cross removes the role: the user is left with « No role ».

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Roles & Permissions ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Contract deadlines
WELCOME.TEXT: How many days before a contract ends and before a trial period ends HR is alerted, for the selected entity and per contract type. The alerts' recipients and wording are set in « Notifications & Emails ».

TABLE.TITLE: Lead times per type
TABLE.TEXT: One row per contract type (CDI, CDD, CIVP, STAGE, FREELANCE, DETACHEMENT), with the contract-end alert's lead time and the trial-end alert's, in days before the deadline.

EDIT.TITLE: Edit lead times
EDIT.TEXT: A row's pencil opens « Alert lead times »: the days before the contract ends (no effect on a CDI, which has no end date) and before the trial period ends (0 = on the day). Each lead time is a whole number from 0 to 365; « Save » confirms.

STATUS.TITLE: Configured or defaults
STATUS.TEXT: « Configured »: the entity has its own lead times for this type. « Defaults »: nothing is saved yet for this type in the entity; « Save » creates its configuration. A change applies from the next daily check, at 08:00.

RUN.TITLE: Run the check
RUN.TEXT: « Run the check now » runs the daily check straight away and shows its summary: alerts due, sent, and with no recipient (retried on the next run). The button only shows with the alert management permission.

END.TITLE: All done!
END.TEXT: You can restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Contract deadlines ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: SharePoint
WELCOME.TEXT: This card links the HR module to the SharePoint tree: where each document kind lives, which documents an employee's dossier must hold, and which SharePoint folder matches each employee. The guide walks through its four tabs.

PATHS.TITLE: Paths by country
PATHS.TEXT: One path per country and document kind. « New path »: the country id, the kind, « Browse » to pick the real folder, then the {employeeFolder} token (and {year} for a kind filed by year), substituted at read time. An invalid path is refused; a path's problems show under it in the table.

REQUIRED.TITLE: Required documents
REQUIRED.TEXT: Pick the country, then switch on « Required » for the documents that make an employee's dossier complete. They drive the « Missing documents » card and the sync; a required document with no path, or sharing its folder with another required document, is not synchronised.

SYNC.TITLE: The sync
SYNC.TEXT: Every night, required documents are read from SharePoint and attached to employees' dossiers. « Sync now » runs it straight away: progress is shown, then the summary (folders read, imported, restored, removed, unreadable or ambiguous).

KIND.TITLE: The document kind
KIND.TEXT: This choice, at the top of the card, sets the kind examined in « Employee mapping » and « Diagnostics », and the kind offered by default for a new path.

EMPLOYEES.TITLE: Employee mapping
EMPLOYEES.TEXT: Each employee's SharePoint folder status, read from the database without calling SharePoint; « Resolve all » queries SharePoint for everyone, which is slow. On a row: « Diagnose », « Pin folder » to enter its exact name when the convention cannot find it, or « Reset » to forget the resolution.

DIAGNOSE.TITLE: Diagnostics
DIAGNOSE.TEXT: Enter a profile id then « Diagnose »: the resulting path, why it failed and the files actually there. A failure is remembered for 24 h; « Force » looks again, for instance after fixing a folder in SharePoint.

END.TITLE: All done!
END.TEXT: You can restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « SharePoint ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Document templates
WELCOME.TEXT: A template is an HTML model specific to the entity, whose variables are replaced with the employee's data when the PDF is generated. Generated certificates and letters use the active template bearing their name.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search and filters
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search a template by name, description or category. « Filters » narrows the list to one category, or also shows inactive templates, hidden by default.

NEW.TITLE: New template
NEW.TEXT: Opens the editor: the name and category (required), an optional description and the SharePoint location. Two templates of the entity cannot share the same name.

CONTENT.TITLE: The HTML content
CONTENT.TEXT: Write the HTML or start from « Template ». Clicking a variable under « Available variables » inserts it at the cursor; « PDF preview » shows the result, with sample data or those of an employee whose profile ID you enter.

TABLE.TITLE: The templates
TABLE.TEXT: Each row shows the category, the number of variables used and the status. The pencil opens the template; the switch deactivates or reactivates it. A template cannot be deleted.

USAGE.TITLE: Templates and generated documents
USAGE.TEXT: For a certificate (employment, salary…), the entity's active template bearing exactly the document's name is used; without it, the built-in standard model is used. If its SharePoint location is filled in, the PDF is also filed there, {employeeFolder} being replaced with the employee's folder.

END.TITLE: All done!
END.TEXT: You can restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Document templates ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Offboarding tasks
WELCOME.TEXT: The catalog sets, for each contract type of the entity, the tasks created automatically when a departure file is opened, with their owner and due date. A change only applies to files opened afterwards.

VALIDATOR.TITLE: The validator role
VALIDATOR.TEXT: Pick the role that gives the HR validation of this entity's departures, then « Save »: only its holders will be able to validate. With « None — standard HR permission », anyone holding the HR offboarding validation or management permission can do it.

TYPES.TITLE: Contract types
TYPES.TEXT: One tab per contract type, taken from the entity's configurable list of contract types (« Configurable lists »). The table shows the selected tab's tasks; the employee's contract type decides which tasks their file gets.

ADD.TITLE: Add a task
ADD.TEXT: The search narrows the shown tab's tasks. « Add a task » asks for the contract type, task code, label, owner role and SLA in working days (at least 1), then the display order. The code, upper-cased, must be unique for the contract type; neither it nor the type can be changed afterwards.

TABLE.TITLE: The tasks
TABLE.TEXT: A row's pencil edits the label, owner, SLA, order and options. The switch deactivates or reactivates the task: an « Inactive » task is no longer added to new files. A task cannot be deleted.

FLAGS.TITLE: SLA, Mandatory and Blocking
FLAGS.TEXT: A task's due date is the file's trigger date plus its SLA in working days (Saturdays and Sundays excluded). A « Blocking » task cannot be skipped and prevents the file's validation until it is completed; an overdue « Mandatory » task flags its stage as blocked.

END.TITLE: All done!
END.TEXT: You can restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Offboarding tasks ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Interview types
WELCOME.TEXT: The interview types (phone, technical, HR…) offered when scheduling a candidate's interview. Each entity has its own list: the one shown is for the entity picked at the top of Administration.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search for a type by label, description, order or status. On the right, reset the sort or choose the columns shown.

NEW.TITLE: New type
NEW.TEXT: « New type » asks for the FR label (required), the display order (suggested after the existing types), the EN label and a description. Without an EN label, the French name is shown in English.

TABLE.TITLE: The types
TABLE.TEXT: Types are listed by display order, with their description under the label. The « Edit » pencil reopens the form to change the labels, the description or the order.

STATUS.TITLE: Activate or deactivate
STATUS.TEXT: A row's switch deactivates or reactivates the type: an inactive type is no longer offered when scheduling. It cannot be deactivated while scheduled interviews use it. A type cannot be deleted.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Interview types ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Notifications & Emails
WELCOME.TEXT: Each HR event (request filed, decision, contract…) can send an in-app notification and an email. Events are defined by the technical team: here you set the channels, the messages and the recipients.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search for an event by module, label or channel (« IN-APP », « EMAIL »). On the right, reset the sort or choose the columns shown.

TABLE.TITLE: The events
TABLE.TEXT: Each row shows the module, the event and its active channels: « IN-APP » for the in-app notification, « EMAIL » for the email. Click an event to open its rule.

END_LIST.TEXT: Open an event, then replay this guide from « Help & guides »: it then presents its routing rule. You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

RULE.TITLE: An open rule
RULE.TEXT: An event's rule decides who is told, through which channel and with which message. If the screen shows « No routing rule », the event sends nothing: click « Create the rule ». In the breadcrumb, « Notifications & Emails » goes back to the list.

GENERAL.TITLE: General settings
GENERAL.TEXT: « In-app notification » and « Email » switch each channel on; they are saved with « Save templates ». « Linked item (deep link) » picks the page opened when the notification is clicked and is saved at once.

TEMPLATES.TITLE: The templates
TEMPLATES.TEXT: The notification's title and body, the email's subject and body. The buttons under each field add a variable, such as {firstName} or {date}, filled in when sending. Click « Save templates » to confirm.

RECIPIENTS.TITLE: The recipients
RECIPIENTS.TEXT: « Add a role », then « Target »: all holders of a role, the manager (higher role), all holders of a permission, the person concerned or their manager. Each addition or removal is saved at once. For the email, at least one « To (TO) » recipient is needed.

TEST.TITLE: Test the rule
TEST.TEXT: « Test the configuration » shows, without sending anything, the messages filled with sample values and the recipients found for your entity. Save your templates before testing.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Notifications & Emails ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Reference data
WELCOME.TEXT: The reference tables used in employee records. Grades, disciplines, NOG levels, departments and banks belong to the entity picked at the top of Administration; nationalities, contract types and IT equipment are shared by all.

TABS.TITLE: The tabs
TABS.TEXT: One tab per reference table: « Grades », « Disciplines », « NOG levels », « Departments », « Banks », « Nationalities », « Contract types », « IT equipment ». Switching tab clears the search and the sort.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search and add
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search for an entry by label, code or order. « Add » opens the form: FR label required, EN label, code and order optional. For a contract type, the code and the FR label are required.

TABLE.TITLE: The entries
TABLE.TEXT: Each row shows the labels, the code, the order and the status. The bin asks for confirmation: the entry is not erased but deactivated, it is no longer offered and the records using it keep it.

NOTICE.TITLE: Default notice period
NOTICE.TEXT: « Grades » tab: the « Default notice period » column gives the starting value of the notice negotiation for that grade (« Not set » in red when missing). The « Edit the default notice period » icon changes it; existing contracts do not change.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Reference data ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Configurable lists
WELCOME.TEXT: The pick lists offered in HR forms: contract type, CSP category, education level, contract end reason… Each value has a code, a French label and an English label.

TABS.TITLE: The lists
TABS.TEXT: One tab per list; the « system » badge marks a list shipped with the application. Click a tab to show its values and its description.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search for a value by its code, its labels or its status. On the right, reset the sort or choose the columns shown.

ADD.TITLE: Add a value
ADD.TEXT: « Add a value » asks for the code, the FR label and the EN label (required) and the display order. The code cannot be changed afterwards. For a list kept per entity, such as « Contract type », the value is created for the entity picked at the top of Administration.

TABLE.TITLE: The values
TABLE.TEXT: The pencil puts the row in edit mode (labels, « Active » box): the tick saves, the cross cancels. An inactive value is no longer offered in forms. On a per-entity list, the « Entity » column tells « All entities » from « This entity ».

SYSTEM.TITLE: System values
SYSTEM.TEXT: A « System » value is used by the application: it can be neither deleted nor deactivated, only its labels can be changed. A contract type already given to employees cannot be deleted either: deactivate it instead.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Configurable lists ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Overtime
WELCOME.TEXT: Each country's overtime calculation rule. The list shows the active rules of every country, not just the selected entity.

SIMULATOR.TITLE: The simulator
SIMULATOR.TEXT: Pick a country, a date, the gross hours and, if needed, the start and end time, then « Simulate ». The result gives normal hours, overtime hours, the rule applied and whether the day is a rest day.

NEW.TITLE: New rule
NEW.TEXT: The country and calculation type are required; then the work start and end time (hour-based types) and the working days. A country has only one active rule: creating one deactivates the previous one.

TYPES.TITLE: Calculation types
TYPES.TEXT: « Weekend only »: every hour worked on a rest day. « Outside normal hours »: time before the start time or after the end time. « Mixed »: both. Rest days are those of the « Entity calendar ».

TABLE.TITLE: The rules
TABLE.TEXT: Each row shows the country, calculation type, normal hours and working week. The pencil edits the rule (the country stays fixed); the switch deactivates it, after confirmation.

END.TITLE: All done!
END.TEXT: You can restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Overtime ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Break management
WELCOME.TEXT: The breaks deducted from employees' working time, in two tabs: « Break templates », specific to each working schedule, and « Legal rules », deduction thresholds valid for the whole entity.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Choosing a regime
TOOLBAR.TEXT: The table shows the templates of one regime only: change it in « Filters ». The search narrows its rows; on the right, reset the sorting or choose the columns shown.

NEW.TITLE: New template
NEW.TEXT: The regime, label and duration are required; then the type, the days, the worked-hours threshold and an optional time range. With a range, only the part of the break during which the employee was working is deducted; without one, the whole duration is, once the threshold is reached.

TABLE.TITLE: The templates
TABLE.TEXT: AUTO and MANDATORY breaks are deducted; an OPTIONAL break never is. « Working days » and « Weekend » follow the entity's weekend. A template cannot be edited: delete it with the bin, then create it again.

LEGAL.TITLE: Legal rules
LEGAL.TEXT: « New rule »: label, minimum hours worked (and optional maximum), deduction in minutes, days, effective date and optional end date. A rule applies to days whose worked hours fall within its range, during its effective period.

LEGAL_TABLE.TITLE: Rules and templates together
LEGAL_TABLE.TEXT: A legal rule is not applied if a break already deducted that day reaches its duration: nothing is counted twice. A row's bin deletes the rule, after confirmation.

END.TITLE: All done!
END.TEXT: You can restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Break management ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Working schedules
WELCOME.TEXT: A regime sets the working hours and days per week. Three tabs: « Catalog » (the entity's regimes), « Role assignment » and « Overview » (the regime applied to each employee).

TIMEZONE.TITLE: The entity's timezone
TIMEZONE.TEXT: All the entity's regime and break times are read in this timezone. Without one, pointage automation is off for its employees: pick it, then « Save ».

CATALOG.TITLE: The catalog
CATALOG.TEXT: Search a regime; « New regime » creates one (code, labels, hours per week, timezone, flexible, default). Click a regime in the list to open it on the right. Badges flag « Default », « Seasonal » and « Flexible ».

EDITOR.TITLE: Editing a regime
EDITOR.TEXT: Hours and days per week, start and end, seasonal period, timezone, flexible hours and overtime, then « Save ». A seasonal regime in progress outranks all the others. The bin stays greyed out while the regime is used by a role or an employee, or is the default regime.

ROLES.TITLE: Assignment by role
ROLES.TEXT: Each role can get a regime, with an effective date and, if needed, an end date. « Assign » or the pencil opens the choice; the bin removes the assignment: the role's employees go back to the default regime. A role without an assignment follows the default regime.

OVERVIEW.TITLE: The overview
OVERVIEW.TEXT: The regime applied to each employee and its source, in order of priority: « Seasonal », « Override », « By role », then « Default ». Search an employee or filter by source; « Unconfigured » shows those with no regime.

OVERRIDE.TITLE: A personal regime
OVERRIDE.TEXT: A row's pencil opens the employee. « Set a personal override » gives them their own regime (effective date, end date or « No end », reason required), which outranks their role's. « Remove override (revert to role) » cancels it.

END.TITLE: All done!
END.TEXT: You can restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Working schedules ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Request types
WELCOME.TEXT: The catalogue of HR requests employees can submit (certificates, personal data updates, bank details…), specific to the selected entity. Only active types are offered to employees.

ACTIONS.TITLE: Initialize or add
ACTIONS.TEXT: « Initialize defaults » creates the standard catalogue for every entity that has no type yet; a catalogue that already has types is left unchanged. « Add » opens the creation of a type.

FORM.TITLE: The type form
FORM.TEXT: Code (upper case, unique within the entity), French and English labels, category, approval level, SLA in days and descriptions. « L2 (double) » requires a second approval after the first one. Once one and a half times the SLA has passed, an alert is sent to the HR manager.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search a type by code, label, category or approval level. On the right, reset the sorting or choose the columns shown.

TABLE.TITLE: The types
TABLE.TEXT: Each row shows the code, label, category, approval (L1 or L2) and SLA. The pencil edits the type; the switch deactivates it, after confirmation: it is no longer offered for new requests and leaves the list.

END.TITLE: All done!
END.TEXT: You can restart this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Request types ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Entity calendar
WELCOME.TEXT: Each entity's weekly rest days. They decide how many days a leave costs, which days presence is expected and how working-time regimes resolve.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Find an entity by name, country code, head count or rest day. On the right, reset the sort or choose the columns.

TABLE.TITLE: The entities
TABLE.TEXT: Only entities with employees or an existing calendar are listed, with their head count and rest days. « Not configured » flags an entity with no setting: the calculation then assumes Saturday and Sunday.

EDIT.TITLE: Configure the calendar
EDIT.TEXT: A row's calendar icon opens « Entity calendar »: choose the « Weekly rest days » (at least one), then « Save ». Notice periods and gaps between leaves are not set here, but per type in « Leave types ».

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Entity calendar ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Leave types
WELCOME.TEXT: The catalogue of leave types offered to employees: what each type debits, its notice periods, its rules and who approves it.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Filters the types on what each row shows: code, label, balance, rules, approvers, state. On the right, reset the sort or choose the columns.

NEW.TITLE: New type
NEW.TEXT: « New type » opens the form: the code (UPPERCASE, digits and _), permanent once created, the FR and EN labels and the display order. The optional explanation is shown to the employee choosing this type.

RULES.TITLE: Balance, notice and approval
RULES.TEXT: « Draws on a balance » asks which balance is debited (CONGE, MALADIE or TELETRAVAIL). The notice and the gap after a leave are counted in working days: empty, the entity's default value applies (no screen sets it); 0, no rule. For a specific delay, enter it in the type. With no approver role, the usual hierarchy approves.

TABLE.TITLE: The catalogue
TABLE.TEXT: Each row sums up the type: its balance (« None » if it debits none), its rules (justification, maximum, notice…), its approvers (« Hierarchy » by default) and its state. The order is that of the list offered to employees.

ACTIONS.TITLE: Edit, deactivate, retire
ACTIONS.TEXT: The pencil opens « Edit type ». The switch activates or deactivates: an inactive type is no longer offered for a new request, but stays in the catalogue. « Retire » first says how many requests use it, then removes it from the catalogue; those requests stay readable and its code can no longer be reused.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Leave types ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Public holidays
WELCOME.TEXT: The public holidays of the entity shown in the header, for the current year. A public holiday is not charged against the leave of that entity's employees; « Switch country » moves to another entity.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: The toolbar
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search by name (French or English) or by date; the search filters the table only. The view icons switch between « Table » and « Calendar ».

ADD.TITLE: Add a public holiday
ADD.TEXT: « Add » opens « New public holiday »: the date, the French label and the English label, then « Create ». Tick « Recurring (every year) » for a fixed-date holiday. An entity has only one public holiday per date.

TABLE.TITLE: The table
TABLE.TEXT: Each row shows the date, the name, the country and whether the holiday recurs. The pencil edits the labels and the recurrence, but not the date: to change it, delete the holiday and create it again. The bin deletes it after confirmation.

CALENDAR.TITLE: The calendar
CALENDAR.TEXT: One month at a time; the arrows change the month. Click a free day to create a public holiday on that date, or a holiday to edit it.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Public holidays ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Payroll settings
WELCOME.TEXT: The payroll parameters of the entity shown in the header: CNSS, IRPP and CSS rates, currency… Each one is a key and a value. For another entity, use « Switch country ».

ACTIONS.TITLE: Add and initialize
ACTIONS.TEXT: « Add » creates a parameter: the key (put in capitals), the value and an optional description, then « Create »; a key exists only once per entity. « Initialize defaults » fills the entities that have no parameter yet with the default values, leaving the others untouched.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Filters the parameters on key, value, description or last-modified date. On the right, reset the sort or choose the displayed columns.

TABLE.TITLE: Edit or delete
TABLE.TEXT: A row's pencil makes the value editable: the tick saves, the cross cancels. Only the value changes, never the key. The bin deletes the parameter after confirmation.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Payroll settings ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Users
WELCOME.TEXT: The register of every DAF360 account: real people as well as technical accounts (tests, imports, service accounts). It is also the only screen where leave balances are entered.

STATS.TITLE: The indicators
STATS.TEXT: « Accounts », « People », « No HR file » and « Never signed in » are counted over the whole register, not over the current search. Each indicator's help explains what it counts.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search and filters
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search by name, email, username or employee ID. « Filter » narrows by account type, entity, role or « Without HR file only ». The view icons switch between « Table » and « Cards ».

CREATE.TITLE: New account
CREATE.TEXT: « New account » asks for the full name, email, role and entity; untick « Account of a real person » for a test or technical account. Sign-in goes through Azure AD on that email address, and no HR file is created.

BALANCES.TITLE: Leave balances
BALANCES.TEXT: Each account shows its leave, sick and remote-work balances. The calendar icon (« Edit balances » in Cards view) opens « Leave balances »: an empty field saves « not recorded » (shown as —), 0 saves « no days left ».

TYPE.TITLE: Person or technical account
TYPE.TEXT: The person icon on a table row reclassifies the account. A technical account disappears from every list of people and every notification recipient list, without being deactivated; the change is passed on straight away to finance and payroll. « Synchronize », in the bar, forces that hand-off for every account.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Administration » tab, « Users ». You will also find this section's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: The candidate list
WELCOME.TEXT: The register of every candidate, as a table, page by page, whatever their status. The board by stage stays on the « Candidates » page.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search and filters
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search by name, email or position. The filters offer the status, position (hiring request or unsolicited application), department and application date.

TABLE.TITLE: The candidates
TABLE.TEXT: A click on a row opens the decision history. « View » opens the candidate's page; for a pending candidate, « Accept » and « Reject » are offered if you have the right.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Candidates » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Create an HR profile
WELCOME.TEXT: This page creates the HR profile of someone who already has a DAF360 account but no file yet. Only the minimum is asked: the rest is completed on the profile afterwards.

HEADER.TITLE: The person
HEADER.TEXT: The account's name, country and role. The « No HR profile » badge recalls that no file exists yet.

FORM.TITLE: The information
FORM.TEXT: On the left, the photo, the full name (required) and the account (email and role, read-only). On the right, the required information — country, contract type, hire date (and end date for a fixed-term contract) — then the position and contact, optional. « Create record » at the bottom.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Profiles » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: File created
WELCOME.TEXT: This page confirms the creation of the employee's file at the end of onboarding: their profile number and the address the welcome email was sent to.

CARD.TITLE: What next?
CARD.TEXT: « View employee profile » opens their HR profile, to complete documents, contracts and equipment. « Back to list » returns to Onboarding.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Onboarding » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: The HR inbox
WELCOME.TEXT: A simple queue of the HR requests to handle, as a table. The menu's inbox page shows the same requests with more tools.

FILTERS.TITLE: The filter
FILTERS.TEXT: Pick « Submitted », « In progress » or « Awaiting L2 », or « All requests ».

TABLE.TITLE: The requests
TABLE.TEXT: Each row shows the employee, type, date and remaining SLA. « Approve » asks for confirmation; « Reject » asks for a reason. « Details » opens the request.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », « Requests » tab. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

UNSAVED.TITLE: Leave without saving?
UNSAVED.MESSAGE: Your changes are not saved. If you leave the page, they will be lost.

WELCOME.TITLE: Welcome to the HR Pipeline
WELCOME.TEXT: This page follows every candidate, from application to hiring. The « New candidate » button, top right, adds one (depending on your rights). Follow this guide to discover the page.

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: « Active candidates » (with the change in applications versus the previous 30 days), « Offer acceptance rate » and « Recruited ». They cover all recruitment: search and filters don't change them.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: Search, filters and display
TOOLBAR.TEXT: Search for a candidate by name. « Filters » lets you pick a status, a position (a recruitment demand or « Spontaneous application »), a department or an application date. The two icons on the right switch between the kanban view and the list view.

BOARD.TITLE: The candidates
BOARD.TEXT: In the kanban view, candidates are arranged in 5 columns: Pending, Accepted, IT & Onboarding, Hired and Rejected. In each column they are sorted by « Fit » score; the arrow in the header reverses the order. Click a card to open the candidate's file.

MOVES.TITLE: Moving a candidate forward
MOVES.TEXT: Drag a card to another column. From « Pending » to « Accepted », the candidate is accepted; to « Rejected », a rejection reason is asked for. From « Accepted » to « IT & Onboarding », you are taken to the IT Provisioning page. From « IT & Onboarding » to « Hired », the candidate's onboarding opens. Any other move is refused, with a message explaining the step to take.

ACTIONS.TITLE: Accept or reject
ACTIONS.TEXT: In the list view (and on mobile), a « Pending » candidate has two icons: ✓ « Accept » (a confirmation is asked for) and ✗ « Reject » (a reason of at least 10 characters is required). They only appear if you are allowed to accept or reject candidates. Click a row to open the file; paging exists in the list view only.

INSIGHTS.TITLE: Recruitment insights
INSIGHTS.TEXT: The « Recruitment insights » tab, on the right edge of the screen, opens a panel with recent activity and the month's recruitment goal.

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », at the bottom of the menu. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Welcome to the profiles directory
WELCOME.TEXT: This page lists the employees in your scope. Follow this guide to learn how to find someone and act on their file.

KPIS.TITLE: The counters
KPIS.TEXT: Total employees, hires over the last 3 months, breakdown by status (active, on leave, on mission) and by contract (CDI, CDD, others). They only follow the Country filter: the search and the other filters leave them unchanged.

SEARCH.TITLE: Search, filters and display
SEARCH.TEXT: Type a name or an email to search. « Advanced filters » filters by country, department, grade, status, contract or hire date. The buttons on the right switch between the grid and the list display.

LIST.TITLE: The employees
LIST.TEXT: Each card shows the country, contract, status and hire date. The eye icon (« View profile ») opens the file; the pencil icon (« Edit ») only appears if you are allowed to edit profiles.

SELECTION.TITLE: Bulk actions
SELECTION.TEXT: Tick one or more cards: a bar appears at the bottom of the screen to export the selection or send a « Bulk Email ». The selection covers the page on screen.

PAGINATION.TITLE: Pagination
PAGINATION.TEXT: Move from page to page and choose how many cards are shown per page (12, 24, 48 or 96).

END.TITLE: All done!
END.TEXT: You can replay this guide at any time from « Help & guides », at the bottom of the menu. You will also find this page's frequently asked questions there.

WELCOME.TITLE: Welcome to the employee's file
WELCOME.TEXT: This file gathers an employee's whole record: identity, employment, contracts, equipment, documents and pay. Follow this guide for a tour; it opens each tab for you.

IDENTITY.TITLE: The identity card
IDENTITY.TEXT: Always visible on the left: photo, name, grade, status, contract, country and the « Identity » block (birth, nationality, ID card, passport, marital status). If you are allowed to edit, the camera icon changes the photo (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 3 MB max).

ACTIONS.TITLE: Actions
ACTIONS.TEXT: At the bottom of the card, depending on your rights: « Change status » (a reason is asked for), « Edit » to switch the file to edit mode, and « Start offboarding », which creates the departure file and takes you there.

EDIT.TITLE: Editing the file
EDIT.TEXT: « Edit » makes the identity and the Employment & role, Contact & Address and Bank details tabs editable. A bar appears at the bottom: enter the « Reason for the change » (required), then « Save changes ». A dot on a tab marks an unsaved change. Switching tabs loses nothing, but « Cancel » or leaving the page discards everything.

TABS.TITLE: Tabs
TABS.TEXT: Each tab is one part of the record; the number shows how many contracts, items or documents it holds. The open tab is kept in the page address: F5 or a shared link reopens the same tab.

EMPLOI.TITLE: Employment & role
EMPLOI.TEXT: The contract (payroll number, hire date, type, end of probation), expectations and pay, the position (department, grade, discipline, NOG level) and the work schedule, read-only. Pay is edited in the Remuneration tab.

CONTACT.TITLE: Contact & Address
CONTACT.TEXT: Personal and work contact details and the address, next to the emergency contact (name, relation, phone).

BANK.TITLE: Bank details
BANK.TEXT: Bank, IBAN, account number, RIB, and the social and tax identifiers (social security, tax ID, CNSS). Only HR managers and administrators see this tab.

CONTRACTS.TITLE: Contracts
CONTRACTS.TEXT: Contracts and their lifecycle: status, probation, notice, days left. Depending on your rights: « New contract », and on an active contract « Validate probation », « Renew CDD », « Convert to CDI » or, for a CIVP, « Request move to CDI ». Below: the contract and transition history.

IT_ASSETS.TITLE: IT equipment
IT_ASSETS.TEXT: Equipment held today and the history. If you manage equipment: « Assign », « Sync » (pulls in what was handed over during IT provisioning), « Return » and the pencil icon « Correct ».

DOCUMENTS.TITLE: Documents
DOCUMENTS.TEXT: The record's documents, grouped by type, with their status (pending, verified, rejected) and expiry warnings. If you are allowed to edit: drop a file (PDF, JPG, PNG) in the « Import a document » area of the right type; the icons on each row verify, reject, edit or remove a document. Files found only in SharePoint are listed separately.

REMUNERATION.TITLE: Remuneration
REMUNERATION.TEXT: Gross salary (with « Calculate net »), current net salary, exceptional bonuses and benefits in kind. This tab is saved on its own, with its own « Save » button and a required « Reason for Change ».

DOC_HISTORY.TITLE: Document history
DOC_HISTORY.TEXT: The employee's whole SharePoint folder, month by month, with a search and filters. « Open » shows the file; the cloud icon opens it in SharePoint. Only HR managers and administrators see it.

DRAWER.TITLE: Generating a certificate
DRAWER.TEXT: The arrow tab on the right edge of the screen opens « HR Documents »: certificates already generated, ready to download, and « Generate » for a work, salary, no-loan, permanent-staff (CDI only) or salary-domiciliation certificate (bank details required).

END.TITLE: You're all set!
END.TEXT: To replay this guide, open « Help & guides » at the bottom of the menu from a file. You will also find the frequently asked questions there.
